meanings.note: With a gerund, presents an action developing over time.

examples.text: Poco a poco hemos ido mejorando.

meanings.note: Marks many specific human direct objects without a separate English word; in poco a poco it belongs to the expression little by little.
Links a clause after a judgment in the first lesson example; introduces a relative clause about people in the second.

examples.trans: I'm looking for people who work here.
You know this suit by heart.

meanings.note: Identity, profession or a characteristic; compare estar for a state or location.
Unstressed direct object; can refer to a statement or idea rather than a masculine physical object.
A desire for a thing or an action.
Affection for a person, as in the lesson.
Also links tratar de + infinitive and forms more than with más de; these uses do not express possession.

examples.text: Llevo más de dos años aquí.
examples.trans: I've been here for more than two years.

meanings.note: Stressed first-person singular pronoun after a preposition. Written with an accent, unlike possessive mi; may be doubled by unstressed me.
Auxiliary before a past participle; does not express possession.
The impersonal present is hay, not ha.

examples.text: ¿La habrá adaptado una chiquita que se llama Hedda Gabler?
examples.trans: Could a young girl called Hedda Gabler have adapted it?

examples.text: En PS nos encantan los nuevos talentos.
examples.trans: At PS we love new talent.

meanings.note: The choice after experto is en; English may use at, in or on according to the following activity or subject.

examples.trans: She is an expert on film.

examples.text: Estamos muy liados, mucho jaleo en la oficina.
examples.trans: We're really swamped, lots of chaos at the office.

meanings.note: Unstressed first-person singular object; its exact direct/indirect/reflexive role depends on the verb.

examples.text: A Macarena nunca le gustó desayunar.
Si lo hiciera bien, dices: "Bueno, pues se ve una pared detrás".
Lidia San José, encantada. Pues me has jodido toda la prueba.

examples.trans: I shot a film in China.
If I hurry, I'll make it.

meanings.note: In estar bien or estar mal, evaluates an action or situation.

examples.text: Pero un punto rojo es como de que no está bien algo.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun; often omitted when the verb already identifies the person.
Before a noun it is a determiner; standing alone, todos/todas can mean everyone or all of them.

examples.text: ¿Qué jaleo ni nada? Si te va genial.
examples.trans: What chaos? Things are going great for you.

examples.text: Venga, vale. Me alegro de verte.

examples.trans: Can you check that socket for me?
She said goodbye from the car.
